items.body:
I have two DatePicker widgets and I am trying to pass the DatePicker values thru the URL when the user changes the DatePicker value, and I am seeing odd behavior. The DatePicker date format toggles between a string and an epoch when I change the other DatePicker. Best shown by example, here are two URLs that are produced when I change each DatePicker,

http://127.0.0.1:6800/?start_date=1529424998666&end_date=Tue%20Jun%2019%202018 http://127.0.0.1:6800/?start_date=Fri%20Jun%2008%202018&end_date=1529512006618

Browser: Chrome
Host OS: Windows 10
Python: 2.7.11

```
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from bokeh.embed import components
from bokeh.models.widgets.inputs import DatePicker
from bokeh.models.callbacks import CustomJS
from bokeh.layouts import column

from flask import Flask

app = Flask(__name__)


@app.route("/", methods=['GET'])
def test():
    text = """<!DOCTYPE html>
    <html lang="en">
    <head>
        <link href="https://cdn.pydata.org/bokeh/release/bokeh-0.12.15.min.css" rel="stylesheet" type="text/css">
        <script src="https://cdn.pydata.org/bokeh/release/bokeh-0.12.15.min.js"></script>
        <link href="https://cdn.pydata.org/bokeh/release/bokeh-widgets-0.12.15.min.css" rel="stylesheet" type="text/css">
        <script src="https://cdn.pydata.org/bokeh/release/bokeh-widgets-0.12.15.min.js"></script>
        <meta charset="UTF-8">
    </head>
    <body>"""

    d_yesterday = datetime.today() - timedelta(days=1)
    d_year_ago = datetime.today() - timedelta(days=365)
    datepicker_start = DatePicker(title="Start Date", min_date=d_year_ago, max_date=datetime.now(), value=d_yesterday)
    datepicker_end = DatePicker(title="End Date", min_date=d_year_ago, max_date=datetime.today(), value=datetime.today())

    all_callback = CustomJS(args=dict(d_start=datepicker_start, d_end=datepicker_end), code="""
        function encodeQueryData(data) {
            let ret = [];
            for (let d in data)
                ret.push(encodeURIComponent(d) + '=' + encodeURIComponent(data[d]));
            return ret.join('&');
        }
        var params = {'start_date': d_start.value, 'end_date': d_end.value }
        var url = '/?' + encodeQueryData(params)
        window.location.replace(url);
    """)
    datepicker_start.callback = all_callback
    datepicker_end.callback = all_callback

    layout = column(datepicker_start, datepicker_end)
    _script, _div = components(layout)
    text += "{}{}".format(_script, _div)

    text += """
    </body></html>
    """

    return text

app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=6800)
```

items.title: datepicker position varies if <div bk-root> is embedded
items.body:
We noticed that the datepicker calendar "jumps away" from the datepicker widget if the bokeh site is embedded elsewhere. We checked that this is no CSS collision.
The cause is the defective calculation of the absolute position of the calendar widget by bokeh in datepicker.coffee. This calculation uses the bk-root-DIV as reference point, not taking into account that the position of the bk-root-DIV may not be to located at <0:0> coordinates.

I would like to fix this. But I have some questions to the makers first:

- I suppose all this fiddling with absolute position is to avoid that the calendar does not pop up at a place out of the current viewport. E.G. if the datepicker widget is near the edge. If this is not the case a relative positioning would be quite easier and more robust.
-  If the former defined use case is truly important I do not understand:
    - Why not use a JS lib like Keep-in-View to accomplish the task?
    - If JS libs are a no go (to keep the codebase small and the dependencies low), why not pin the 
calender to the viewport instead.

items.title: Datepicker returns one day earlier than picked in IE
items.body:
Using datepicker in FF and IE revelas. The returned date from IE is one day earlier than selected.
Example. Selected is 23.09.2017T00:00:00GMT+2: -> FF 23.09.2017, IE 22.09.2017.
The date.ToISOString() functions behaves differently on FF and IE. In FF only the date part is used -> "22.09.2017". IE takes into account the timezone (in this case Europe/Berlin GMT+2) and shifts the time to UTC before calculating the ISO-String. So 23.09.2017:00:00:00GMT+2 becomes 22.09.2017 22:00:00UTC -> "22.09.2017".
Fix will be to change : 
```
  _on_select: (date) =>
    @model.value = date.toISOString()
    @change_input()
```
to  :
```
  _on_select: (date) =>
    @model.value = date.getFullYear().toString()+'-'+date.getMonth().toString()+'-'+date.getDate().toString() 
    @change_input()
```
If this is OK for everybody then I will prepare a PR

items.title: Changing the min_date of a DatePicker in a js callback
items.body:
I'm trying to control the min_date of a DatePicker with another DatePicker and a js callback. The idea being that I can allow a user to select a date range but not be able to select a start after the end or an end before the start.

Here's my code:
```
from datetime import datetime

import bokeh
from bokeh.io import output_file, show, reset_output
from bokeh.models import CustomJS
from bokeh.models.widgets import DatePicker
from bokeh.layouts import row

print('Bokeh version:', bokeh.__version__)
reset_output()
output_file("test.html")

start_picker = DatePicker(title="Start",
                    min_date=datetime(2018, 1, 10),
                    max_date=datetime(2018, 1, 31),
                    value=datetime(2018, 1, 1))

end_picker = DatePicker(title="End",
                    min_date=datetime(2018, 1, 10),
                    max_date=datetime(2018, 1, 31),
                    value=datetime(2018, 1, 15))


start_picker_callback = CustomJS(args=dict(end_picker=end_picker), code=f"""
    var min_date = Date.parse(Date(cb_obj.value));
    console.log('Selected start:', min_date)
    console.log('Old end_picker.min_date =', end_picker.min_date)
    
    end_picker.min_date = min_date;
    console.log('New end_picker.min_date =', end_picker.min_date)
    
    end_picker.change.emit();
""")
start_picker.js_on_change('value', start_picker_callback)

layout = row(start_picker, end_picker)
show(layout)
```

From the console.log(...) calls the callback appears to be changing the value of end_picker's min_date. However when you try to select an end date (after changing the start date), there has been no change. 

However, if I follow the same logic with Sliders it works:
```
from datetime import datetime

import bokeh
from bokeh.io import output_file, show, reset_output
from bokeh.models import CustomJS
from bokeh.models.widgets import Slider
from bokeh.layouts import row

print('Bokeh version:', bokeh.__version__)
reset_output()
output_file("test.html")

slider1 = Slider(title="Slider 1",
                 start=1,
                 end=5,
                 value=3,
                 step=1)

slider2 = Slider(title="Slider 2",
                 start=1,
                 end=10,
                 value=6,
                 step=1)


slider_callback = CustomJS(args=dict(slider2=slider2), code="""
    var min_num = cb_obj.value;
    console.log('Selected number:', min_num)
    console.log('Old slider2.start =', slider2.start)
    
    slider2.start = min_num;
    console.log('New slider2.start =', slider2.start)
    
    slider2.change.emit();
""")
slider1.js_on_change('value', slider_callback)

layout = row(slider1, slider2)
show(layout)
```
Is this a bug or is there something I am doing wrong or some way to get around it?

Also a DatePicker for ranges would be cool!
Something like this:

items.title: [BUG] DatePicker display off-by-one in non-GMT timezone after upgrade to 1.4.0
items.body:
Versions:

- Bokeh: 1.4.0
- Python: 3.7.3
- Chrome: 78.0.3904.108 (Official Build) (64-bit)
- O/S: Windows 7 Pro SP1
- **TimeZone**: EST (Issue observed in EST but not in GMT)

After the fix of [this issue](https://github.com/bokeh/bokeh/pull/9232/commits/472e4770d363b3914bb478f0a6c3a83787b20c0d#) in 1.4, I observe the following issue;

In the EST timezone, if I update a DatePicker based on the value of another DatePicker, I get a different date (1 day previous to the selected date).  If the browser is located in a GMT timezone then I do not observe the issue.  Minimal example below.

**Expected behavior**: On selecting a date from the first DatePicker, the second DatePicker displays that same date;

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7271339/70002782-16e56500-152f-11ea-9f05-3b810742904f.png)


**Observed behavior**: On selecting a date from the first DatePicker, the second DatePicker shows a date one day previous to the selected date;

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7271339/70002817-354b6080-152f-11ea-9c39-ad09e0b5ca05.png)

```
from bokeh.layouts import column
from bokeh.models import DatePicker
from bokeh.plotting import curdoc


def a_changed(attr, old, new):
    date_picker_b.value = new


date_picker_a = DatePicker()
date_picker_b = DatePicker()

# When we pick a date in date_picker_a, set the date in date_picker_b
date_picker_a.on_change('value', a_changed)

curdoc().add_root(column(date_picker_a, date_picker_b))

```

In our application, we have a date slider and some fixed date-range buttons (year-to-date, month-to-date etc) coupled to two date pickers, which is how we observed the issue, but the above example seems to minimally demonstrate the issue that dates don't round-trip from the DatePickers.
